title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows
author: Ayesha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s security and compliance controls and operational procedures for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC requirements, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection and workflows, and risk & exception handling. It is intended for engineers, security reviewers, and compliance owners who implement or verify controls for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood services and managed customer deployments (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Includes platform control plane, serving runtime, telemetry pipelines, and customer-managed components when under Redwood support.
- Excludes third-party vendor controls (see vendor assessments for those artifacts).

Owner & Contacts
- Document owner: security@redwood.com (Ayesha Patel)
- On-call for security incidents: sec-oncall@redwood.com
- Audit evidence requests: compliance-requests@redwood.com

RBAC & Authentication
Purpose: Prevent unauthorized access to production systems and customer data by enforcing least privilege and strong authentication.

Roles and role hierarchy
- org-admin: Full organization-level administrative privileges (restricted to >2 admins for live environments).
- infra-operator: Can manage infra resources (EC2/GKE nodes, capacity pools) but not customer data exports.
- service-admin: Manage service config, rollouts, and runbooks for an individual service.
- security-reader: Read-only access to security dashboards, audit logs, and IAM policies.
- security-admin: Elevated privileges for investigations (temporary approvals required).
- customer-admin: Customer-facing admin used in Dedicated/Private deployments and scoped by customer tenancy.

Authentication and federation
- All human users authenticate via SSO (Okta). SAML assertion mapping to internal roles is defined in auth-service config.
- Service-to-service uses mTLS + JWT (short-lived) issued by redwood-token-issuer.
- Admin console requires enforced MFA (hardware token recommended).

Policy enforcement and tooling
- Primary enforcement: authz-service (policy engine) is consulted for every sensitive action (write to audit-store, change ACLs, create rollout).
- Policy format: Rego (OPA). Policies stored in git, change-reviewed, and deployed via policy-ci pipeline.
- Authorization failure behavior: deny-by-default; failures generate a high-severity audit event and an alert if the request is from a privileged principal.

Audit Logging
Goals: Provide a complete, tamper-evident trail for access and configuration changes across the control plane and runtime.

What we log
- Authentication events: login, logout, SSO assertions, MFA challenges and failures.
- Authorization decisions: principal, resource, action, policy id, decision (allow/deny), request metadata (IP, region).
- Configuration changes: deployments, feature flags, RBAC policy updates, infra changes.
- Data access events: dataset reads/exports, customer data access by support or engineering.
- Elevated workflows: temporary privilege grants and approvals.

Architecture and flow
1. Services emit structured audit events to local audit-agent (JSON schema v1.2).
2. audit-agent forwards to kafka-audit-topic (encrypted in transit).
3. audit-ingest pipeline validates, enriches (user-id, request-id), and sinks to both:
   - Write-once S3 bucket: s3://redwood-audit-immutable (immutability policy + versioning enabled)
   - BigQuery audit datasets for interactive queries (access restricted)

SLOs & retention
- Delivery SLO: 99.9% of audit events available in BigQuery within 60s of generation.
- Integrity SLO: Weekly checksum verification across write-once buckets; any drift triggers incident.
- Retention: enterprise customers: 7 years (configurable); standard: 365 days. See "Data Residency & Retention" for details.

Tamper-evidence and protections
- S3 buckets: Object Lock in governance mode + server-side encryption with CMKs (redwood-kms).
- Write pipeline: append-only design; no direct write permissions to audit S3 buckets outside of audit-ingest service account.
- Periodic snapshot + hash published to internal transparency log and stored off-site.

Example query
- BigQuery: SELECT * FROM `redwood-prod.audit.events` WHERE principal = 'alice@example.com' AND event_time >= '2026-03-01' ORDER BY event_time DESC LIMIT 100;

Data Residency & Retention
Principles
- Customers choose a region for customer data residency (us-east1, europe-west2, ap-southeast1 for supported customers).
- Control plane metadata is stored in us-east1 by default; for Private deployments, control plane may be customer-hosted per contract.

Retention policies (summary table)
| Data type                  | Default retention | Enterprise option | Storage location examples       |
|---------------------------|-------------------:|-------------------:|---------------------------------|
| Audit logs                | 1 year             | up to 7 years      | s3://redwood-audit-immutable    |
| Access logs (LB, proxy)   | 90 days            | 1 year             | cloud-logs / central logging    |
| KV cache & runtime state  | 30 days            | n/a                | encrypted object stores         |
| Traces & metrics (high-res)| 30 days (raw), 1 year (rollup)| n/a | telemetry cluster (region scoping)|

Cross-region replication
- Enterprise customers with residency requirements: audit and access logs are kept in the customer-specified region and replication is disabled unless contractually allowed.

Data deletion and exports
- Data deletion follows an irreversible workflow: a deletion request ticket is required, approver from Legal & Security must sign off, and deletion is audited.
- Exports (for support) require customer consent or a valid legal request; exports are logged and stored with retention policy aligned with export reason.

Secure SDLC Requirements
Summary: Security gates embedded into CI/CD to prevent vulnerable code from reaching production.

Must-have controls
1. Static analysis: All repos must run SAST on pull requests (Snyk/CodeQL) with policy-based block on high-severity results.
2. Dependency scanning: SBOM generation for services and image build pipelines; block if critical CVE present without mitigations.
3. Secret scanning: Prevent leaked keys in PRs (pre-merge hook + post-commit detection).
4. IaC policy checks: Terraform plans validated against infra-standards (conftest/Rego).
5. Change approval: Production infra or policy changes require two approvers (one from service owner, one from infra/security).
6. Canary & gradual rollout: Feature rollouts default to 10% canary for 24h before full release; rollback automation on SLO regressions.

Required artifacts for release
- SBOM (software bill of materials) and image digests
- SAST and dependency scan report (pass/fail status)
- Deployment runbook and rollback steps
- Security review checklist (completed or waived with reason and approval)

Incident Response — Security Procedures
High-level goals: detect, contain, eradicate, recover, and provide evidence for forensic review.

Playbook summary (for security incidents)
1. Detection & Triage\   - Alerts land in security-splunk and PagerDuty sec-oncall.\   - Triage team classifies: data exposure, service compromise, misconfiguration, or suspicious access.
2. Containment\   - Short-term: rotate affected credentials, revoke sessions, isolate instances/containers, enforce firewall rules.\   - Long-term: apply patches, configuration changes, and perform broader scans.
3. Forensics & Evidence Preservation\   - Snapshot affected instances, preserve relevant audit logs and network captures to s3://redwood-forensics (write-once).\   - Formal chain-of-custody recorded in incident ticket.
4. Notification & Escalation\   - Internal: Notify CTO, CISO, legal, customer-success for impacted customers.\   - External: Follow notification timelines in SLA and regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR 72-hour window).
5. Remediation & Postmortem\   - Implement fixes, validate via test harness and monitoring.\   - Postmortem authored within 7 days; include root cause, blast radius, mitigations, and follow-ups with owners and deadlines.

Prescribed tooling and artifacts
- Forensic snapshot steps (CLI):
  1) aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-xxxx --description "incident-2026-03-01-<id>"
  2) gcloud compute disks snapshot my-disk --snapshot-names "incident-2026-03-01-<id>"
- Audit bundle export: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(token)" "https://audit-api.redwood.internal/v1/exports?incident_id=<id>" -o /tmp/incident-<id>-audit.json

Compliance Evidence Workflows
Objective: Provide repeatable, auditable evidence to internal and external audits (SOC2, ISO27001).

Evidence categories and owners
- IAM & RBAC evidence: security (owner) — policy git history, SSO configuration screenshots, role mappings.
- Audit logs: infra (owner) — immutable S3 exports, BigQuery snapshots.
- SDLC controls: eng-developer-experience (owner) — CI logs, scan reports, SBOMs.
- Incident records: security & eng-sre (owner) — incident tickets, forensics bundles, remediation evidence.

Typical request workflow
1. Request submitted to compliance-requests@redwood.com with evidence type and timeframe.
2. Compliance owner validates scope and opens a tracked ticket (JIRA ID).
3. Evidence package compiled via automated exporter scripts and uploaded to secure share (link logged in ticket).
4. Reviewer signs off; artifacts are checksum-verified and recorded in evidence register.

Automation tips and scripts
- evidence-exporter: internal tool that accepts artifact type and timeframe and produces a signed zip with checksums. Example: ./evidence-exporter --type audit_logs --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-02-01 --out /tmp/audit-evidence.zip

Risk & Exceptions Process
When a control cannot be met (technical limitation, customer constraint, or timing), a documented exception is required.

Exception request process
1. Submit exception RFC (git repo exceptions/ or JIRA) with: impacted control, risk assessment, compensating controls, duration, and remediation plan.
2. Security reviews and assigns risk rating (Low / Medium / High).
3. Approval: low-risk auto-approved by Security Lead; medium & high risk require CISO + Legal sign-off and board notification for high risk.
4. Exceptions logged in the Risk & Exceptions register with an expiration date and remediation owner.

Example compensating controls
- If audit-forwarding to a central region is blocked by residency, require per-region immutable stores and daily digest checksums forwarded to central security account.

Appendices
A. Audit event JSON schema (summary)
{
  "event_time": "ISO8601",
  "principal": "user or service",
  "action": "string",
  "resource": "string",
  "decision": "allow|deny",
  "policy_id": "string",
  "request_id": "UUID"
}
